name: Dub Narcotic Sound System
label: K
lede: Calvin Johnson took the melodica out of Beat Happening, put a dub echo on it, and spent a decade making party records in his own basement studio, once with the Jon Spencer Blues Explosion showing up with nothing but guitars.

eras.title: A basement, a melodica, an echo
eras.text: Beat Happening had gone quiet, and Calvin Johnson had a studio in the basement of his own label. Dub Narcotic Sound System is what came out of it: a dub mindset applied to rock, not to reggae.

years.src: Wikipedia: K Records · Tape Op: Calvin Johnson, The K Records Studio
years.h: Johnson turns a basement into Dub Narcotic Studio
years.p: [[Calvin Johnson|cac7a688-14a8-46c3-8fc8-11cca866677c]] converts a basement space in Olympia into a recording room, and names it after the sound he wants to make.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia's K Records entry, the studio dates to 1993 and later moved into the Olympia Knitting Mills building, where it picked up a 16-track tape machine and doubled as K Records offices and housing for musicians.

In a Tape Op interview, Johnson described a room about 110 by 45 feet with no clock in it, where bands mostly recorded for free. Tape Op dates his move into that building to 1988, so the timeline is fuzzy.

years.src: Trouser Press: Dub Narcotic Sound System
years.h: Hands on the Dial: dub and toast versions of old singles
years.p: A cassette of dub and toasted remakes of earlier material, recorded while [[Beat Happening|449e44cb-bcae-4c48-a1af-5d8df0f81456]] sat on hiatus.
years.xp: Trouser Press calls the tape "enjoyable, if not necessary", and describes the project's premise: sparse arrangements and talk-sung vocals over backing tracks, with dub production techniques applied to rock.

years.src: Trouser Press: Dub Narcotic Sound System
years.h: Industrial Breakdown EP: one song, several ways
years.p: The title track appears in multiple versions alongside instrumental dubs and rewrites of existing material.
years.xp: Trouser Press describes it as the record that set the pattern: a single idea stretched into versions and dubs, the way a reggae 12-inch would do it, minus the reggae.

years.src: Trouser Press: Dub Narcotic Sound System
years.h: Ridin' Shotgun, cut in Memphis, gets a rough review
years.p: Trouser Press calls its three grooves "fairly dull" and the project's weakest effort.
years.xp: The same guide is kinder to Echoes From the Scene Control Room, the 1995 vinyl-only debut LP of mostly instrumentals and melodica showcases built on previously recorded backing tracks.

years.src: Trouser Press: Dub Narcotic Sound System
years.h: Johnson tours and records with the Dead Presidents hip-hop crew
years.p: The collaboration yields the Spread Butter EP, which pairs an Olympia indie label boss with a rap crew.
years.xp: Trouser Press credits Johnson with working with the Dead Presidents both on tour and in the studio, and lists Spread Butter as a 1995 result.

eras.title: Boot Party
eras.text: The dub gets funkier and a band shows up. A real rhythm section, two singers and a turntablist turn a studio project into something people can dance to.

years.src: Wikipedia: Boot Party · Trouser Press: Dub Narcotic Sound System
years.p: Ten tracks, 42 minutes, an 8-minute title song, and Lois Maffeo and Jen Smith on vocals.
years.xp:
Per Wikipedia, the band on Boot Party was Larry Butler on drums, Lindy Coyne and Brian Weber on guitars (Weber also on organ), Todd Ranslow on bass, DJ Sayeed on turntables, and Johnson on melodica. The album opens with "Test Pattern" and closes with the 8:06 title track.

Trouser Press hears a move away from heavy dub toward a "60s R&B stride", bathing in a "stoned soul picnic" atmosphere.

years.src: Trouser Press: Dub Narcotic Sound System
years.h: [[Lois Maffeo|ab9605b4-3ef8-4dde-99c4-87abe0f769a2]] gets her own EP: Ship to Shore
years.p: Maffeo, a guest on Boot Party, is now the featured artist.
years.xp: Trouser Press calls the production on Ship to Shore "seductive and surprisingly slick", a long way from the basement dubs of 1994.

eras.title: Sideways Soul
eras.text: The Jon Spencer Blues Explosion owed Johnson a favor and Johnson knew what he wanted for it. Two bands from opposite coasts ended up in one Olympia room.

q: They pulled up and looked out of the car like, 'Is this the place?'
years.src: The Stranger: Dub Narcotic Blues Explosion · The A.V. Club: Dub Narcotic Meets Jon Spencer Blues Explosion in a Dancehall Style · Bandcamp: Sideways Soul (KLP103)
years.h: The Blues Explosion pays a debt in Johnson's studio
years.p: Jon Spencer, Judah Bauer and Russell Simins arrive in Olympia owing Johnson a remix payment; he asks for a session instead.
years.xp:
The A.V. Club dates the setup to 1995: Johnson remixed a Blues Explosion track for their Experimental Remixes EP, and asked to be paid in studio time. The Stranger says the session lasted two days, with the Blues Explosion showing up with guitars and little else.

Johnson handed Bauer his prized Fender Vibrochamp, then evened things out by giving Spencer's guitarist a very large microphone. The two bands traded freestyle lines about Olympia's people and places.

years.src: Tinnitist: Classic Album Review, Dub Narcotic Sound System, Out Of Your Mind
yt: Dub Narcotic Sound System, Fuck Shit Up
years.h: Out of Your Mind: a second full-length, mostly party
years.p: K's Stax-and-basement-funk stew, with Johnson's croak out front.
years.xp: Darryl Sterdan, reviewing it, wrote that the Dub Narcotic approach "will never be stylish. Which, if you ask me, is a damn shame." His review describes "a trashy party mix of Stax/Volt soul, basement funk jams" with Johnson's voice as a "laconic, creaking croak."

years.src: The A.V. Club: Dub Narcotic Meets Jon Spencer Blues Explosion in a Dancehall Style · Bandcamp: Sideways Soul (KLP103) · Discogs: Sideways Soul
years.p: Nine tracks, including a 9:50 "Fudgy the Whale" that lists Olympia karaoke dances.
years.xp:
The A.V. Club calls it "a party album" pairing Johnson's croon with the Blues Explosion's bar-blues. The tracklist runs "Banana Version," "Love Ain't On The Run," "Banana Meltdown," "Chicken Legs" and "Calvin's On A Bummer", among others.

Discogs credits Spencer on guitar, voice and organ, Bauer on guitar, Simins on drums, and Phil Elverum and Brian Weber on auxiliary engineering.

eras.title: Handclappin' and a new engineer
eras.text: After four years of quiet on the DNSS front, a van crash and a new record with a new hand at the board.

years.p: Wikipedia's discography lists it on K in 2003, the first DNSS release since Sideways Soul.

years.h: A van crash in Montana injures Johnson on tour
years.p: According to Wikipedia, the 2003 tour crash left Johnson with a concussion and a speech impediment.

years.src: Bandcamp: Degenerate Introduction (KLP157) · Tape Op: Calvin Johnson, The K Records Studio
years.h: Degenerate Introduction: Chris Sutton and Heather Dunn
years.p: Adam Forkner engineers it, and Johnson does not.
years.xp:
Bandcamp lists the album as nine tracks recorded at Dub Narcotic Studios, with Johnson on vocals, guitar, melodica and percussion, Chris Sutton on bass, drums, guitar and organ, and Heather Dunn on vocals, bass, sax and drums. It was the first full-length since 1998's Out of Your Mind.

The Tape Op interview notes that the newer single was engineered by Adam Forkner instead of Johnson.
